input.prompt: An authentic Srikalahasti kalamkari hand-painted cotton textile, a long horizontal border band, photographed flat and straight-on so the painted cloth fills the entire frame edge to edge with no margin. Subject: the sea at Visakhapatnam. Rows of stylised rolling waves in indigo blue with curling ecru crests, outlined in black, fill the whole band. Swimming among the waves: several patterned fish with scale fills and one crab. Riding the waves are two traditional wooden fishing catamarans (teppa), each a few lashed logs with a single patterned triangular sail filled with stripes and dots, no people aboard. Along the top edge runs a line of rounded green hills with dotted fills, and a round myrobalan-yellow sun with petal-shaped rays sits above the hills, set against a deep madder-red sky. A thin band of dots runs along the very top edge and another along the very bottom edge. The scene continues off both the left and right ends with no border, no frame and no edge decoration at the left or right. Style: match the reference image exactly in palette, line quality, fill patterns and cotton texture. Freehand kalam (bamboo pen) outlines in iron-black with confident, slightly irregular line weight; flat natural vegetable-dye fills only: deep madder red (brick red), indigo blue, myrobalan-turmeric yellow, green made from indigo over yellow, and undyed ecru cotton; dense hand-drawn fill patterns of dots, cross-hatching, scales and tiny petals; visible hand-woven cotton weave and slight dye bleed at the edges of colour areas. Completely flat, no perspective, no shading, no gradients, no metallic gold, no 3D, no photorealism. No text, no letters, no writing, no numbers, no signature, no lamps, no diyas, no candles, no fire, no flames.
